headlines.headline: JAMES HARDEN AGREES TO RETURN TO CAVALIERS ON THREE-YEAR, $97M DEAL
headlines.detail: Harden is heading back to Cleveland on a three-year deal with a player option for 2028-29, part of a busy free-agency stretch that also saw DeMar DeRozan agree to join Denver (recruited by Nikola Jokic, Aaron Gordon and Jamal Murray), the Trail Blazers land Ja Morant in a trade with Memphis, and Draymond Green re-sign with Golden State for one year, $27.7 million.

headlines.headline: PRESEASON WEEK 2 ROSTER-BUBBLE BATTLES HIT FRIDAY NIGHT
headlines.detail: Three games Friday: Jets at Steelers (Will Howard starting for Pittsburgh with rookie Drew Allar to follow), Panthers at Jaguars, and Packers at Broncos (Bo Nix set to see action at Mile High). It follows Thursday's doubleheader where Justin Herbert ran the Chargers' first-team offense for one drive and Texans WR Jayden Higgins was lost for the season to a torn ACL.

headlines.headline: OKLAHOMA EXTENDS VENABLES THROUGH 2031 AHEAD OF SEASON
headlines.detail: Oklahoma has signed head coach Brent Venables to a contract extension running through the 2031 season, locking in stability heading into fall camp. Alabama's QB battle between five-star Keelon Russell and Austin Mack remains unsettled as camp winds down, and SEC media is coalescing around Georgia as the conference favorite given Texas's brutal 2026 schedule.

headlines.headline: SEC COMMISSIONER SANKEY FIGHTS TO BLOCK ATHLETE'S RETURN-TO-COLLEGE BID
headlines.detail: SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey filed an affidavit in Louisiana court asking a judge to uphold NCAA rules barring athletes who signed pro contracts from returning to college eligibility, in response to a lawsuit from LSU signee and former NBA G-League player RJ Luis. Santa Clara's Elijah Mahi is returning for a fifth season, and Murray State-NC State and Seton Hall-Wisconsin headline the Baha Mar Hoops Bahamas Championship field.
